source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Russian spelling is fairly regular once you know which syllable is stressed. Stress changes how the vowels sound, so learn it along with each word.
reading: CAPITALS mark the stress. Russian stress can fall anywhere and isn't marked in normal writing.
"y" on its own (vy, ty, byl) means the ы sound, not "why".
"yeh", "nyet" and "gdyeh" mean the consonant is soft (see below).

sounds.symbol: Р Н В С У Х
sounds.name: Letters that lie
sounds.spelled: r, n, v, s, oo, kh
sounds.how: They look like Latin letters but sound different: Р = r, Н = n, В = v, С = s, У = oo, Х = kh. Also Е = ye and Я = ya.

sounds.name: Yery
sounds.how: Start saying "ee", then pull your tongue back and relax your lips. It sits between the i in "bit" and the u in "put".

sounds.symbol: ь  е ё и ю я
sounds.name: Soft consonants
sounds.how: Before these letters, a consonant is made with the middle of your tongue raised, which adds a faint y: Нет is "nyet", not "net".

sounds.name: Unstressed O
sounds.how: An o that isn't stressed sounds like "ah", or a weak "uh" further from the stress. Only the stressed о sounds like "oh".

sounds.name: Unstressed E / Ya
sounds.how: When they aren't stressed, е and я shrink toward a short "ee": дела is "dee-LAH".

sounds.name: Kha
sounds.how: Like the ch in Scottish "loch", but softer than the Arabic or Hebrew sound.

sounds.name: Er
sounds.how: A tapped or lightly rolled r made with the tip of the tongue, as in Spanish or Italian.

sounds.name: Hushing sounds
sounds.how: ж = zh as in "measure", ш = a hard sh, щ = a longer, softer sh (shch), ч = ch. Exception: in что, ч is said as sh ("shtoh").

sounds.name: Final devoicing
sounds.how: At the end of a word, or before a voiceless consonant, voiced letters turn voiceless: д sounds like t, в like f.
